## rebar-debug RCA — NOT-A-BUG (working-as-designed; duplicate of the concurrent-writer unpushed-count misread)

Investigated per the /rebar-debug protocol on current `origin/main` (`de8801d13d3d`). **No code change is warranted.** The reported premise ("no fetch+retry, silently growing an unpushed backlog / lost history") is contradicted by shipped code and by a real diverged-remote reproduction. All four acceptance criteria are already satisfied by merged work.

### Proven root cause of the observed symptom
The `push_status.state:"pending"` + `reason:"final-push-rejected"` with a growing `unpushed` count (9→30) is the **documented, best-effort, self-healing terminal outcome of the tickets-branch CAS push under sustained concurrent-writer contention** — not a missing retry loop and not lost writes.

- The auto-push path **already fetches + merges + retries** on a non-fast-forward: `push_tickets_branch` → `_recover_non_fast_forward` (`src/rebar/_store/push_recovery.py`) does a union fetch+merge before a bounded retry — five push-first CAS cycles plus one terminal push after a clean fifth merge (`src/rebar/_store/push.py:249-333`). Authoritative contract: `docs/concurrency.md:551` — *"On a non-fast-forward rejection, `push_tickets_branch` … fetches and merges the remote tickets branch as a union before a bounded retry. Push is best-effort by default. A failed push … does not fail existing callers. It warns and preserves local commits. … Existing callers inherit five push-first recovery cycles and one final push after a clean fifth merge."*
- The growing `unpushed` count is **local merge topology ahead of the remote ref**, which rises under concurrent writes even when all content has landed. Bug `3ff9` (squeamish-halfawake-fantail) already reworded the message to state the self-healing contract ("committed locally, they publish on the next successful push") and keys the log LEVEL on `backlog_grew` — a **non-growing** contention loss is INFO/expected/self-healing; only sustained growth escalates to WARNING (`src/rebar/_store/push_state.py:115-149`).

### Proof (real diverged-remote reproduction; non-determinism handled)
Drove `push_tickets_branch` against **real temporary git repos** (bare origin + tracker clone + a concurrent-writer clone), never the shared `origin/tickets`. Contention was made **deterministic** via an injected `sleep_fn` barrier that advances the remote on every CAS backoff cycle (no timing dependence):

- **[A] Single diverged remote →** push runs fetch+merge+retry, **content lands on the remote** (`push_status=ok`, `ahead=0`). Directly refutes "no fetch+retry."
- **[B] Sustained contention →** reproduces the ticket exactly: `push_status=pending`, `reason=final-push-rejected`, `unpushed` grew 3→8, no error raised, **local commits intact**.
- **[B] Contention subsides →** one uncontended push **drains the entire backlog**: `all_content_landed=True`, `push_status=ok`, `ahead=0`. **Nothing was lost; it self-healed** on the next write — exactly the documented contract.

The discriminating outcome: a genuine "no fetch+retry / lost writes" defect would show content never landing or the backlog never draining; instead the loop reconciles, lands content when it can, and a transient contention loss self-heals with zero loss.

### Acceptance criteria are already met by merged work
- **AC1 (root-cause the sequence):** done above — expected terminal reason of the best-effort CAS budget under contention.
- **AC2 (fetch + rebase/ff-merge retry loop):** already shipped — `meagre-grassgreen-waterdogs` / `deft-elaborate-pug`, merged `a8e0f67c827706525becb9b4d3df8a4da738d44e`; lives in `push.py`/`push_recovery.py`.
- **AC3 (caller can detect a persistently pending push_status):** already shipped — `vapoury-attack-lamb` (RC-3) delivered the durable pending marker (`src/rebar/_store/push_state.py`) and the MCP `push_status` write-tool field. This is literally how the reporter observed the condition, so detection demonstrably works; `rebar fsck` also reports `PUSH_PENDING`.
- **AC4 (reject-then-retry test):** already present — `tests/unit/test_push_rejection_surfacing.py`, `tests/unit/test_push_callers_best_effort.py` (real bare-origin rejection, five in-loop pushes + terminal push, best-effort no-raise).

### Classification
`duplicate` of `byzantine-colourless-redpoll` (`a197-d055-…`, closed **not_a_bug/WITHDRAWN**), which litigated the identical "backlog grows under concurrent writers" misread: the reporter there used `git rev-list --count origin/tickets..HEAD` as a proxy for unpushed work, watched it rise under load, and confirmed on direct check that **every write had actually landed on the remote**. Same mechanism here; the only addition is the `final-push-rejected` per-write reason, which is itself the documented self-healing terminal outcome.

No `caused_by` attribution — there is no defect to attribute (not-a-bug guard). No fix landed; no `--force` used. The behavior is the documented best-effort sync contract; changing it to a blocking/strict default would alter documented sync semantics and is out of scope (would be an ESCALATE, not an auto-fix — but no change is needed here).
